messages:
Ashley: quick follow-up on the RFC about multi-head attention memory layouts — we need a concrete kernel handoff plan for packed QKV (contiguous) vs per-tensor/per-head layouts. who wants to own the handoff?
Erin: I can take ownership of the microbench sweep. early findings: packed-contiguous helps for fused kernels up to seq=512, beyond that stride/tiling wins. cache thrash point around head_dim=64 when seq>768.
Dave: can you paste the shapes/config you used? different batch/seq mixes change the crossover a lot.
Erin: sure, sample shapes we ran:
```
B=8, S=256/512/1024, H=16, D=64
packed_qkv: [B, S, 3, H, D]  # contiguous qkv axis
separate: Q: [B, S, H, D], K:..., V:...
```
Priya: FYI: on Ampere the packed layout lets the fused kernel read fewer loads per token, but it's very sensitive to alignment and stride. if the QKV pack isn't 128-bit-aligned we lose vectorization.
Tom: proposal: we add a KernelPolicy layer in the runtime that maps request shapes -> preferred kernel + layout transform plan. policy table lives in runtime config and can be hot-reloaded.
Ashley: +1. needs to expose: prefer_fused, prefer_per_head, reorder_cost_threshold, max_seq_len_pref.
Erin: also need a safe fallback that doesn't re-layout to an incompatible memory format if caller pinned buffer semantics. maybe a flag preserve_layout=true that skips transformations and forces a kernel that supports incoming layout.
Dave: ops-wise, re-layout is ~0.4ms for S=512,B=8,H=16 — often cheaper than a suboptimal kernel for many tokens but not for latency-sensitive 1-2 token cases.
Priya: question — do we want to mandate a canonical on-disk/onnx layout for model imports? it would simplify kernel matching but hurts model portability.
Tom: I'd prefer model-import standard + runtime override. import-time we annotate preferred_layout and add a lightweight shim that can rewrite if runtime policy says so.
infra-bot: buildkite/pipeline:kernel-selector smoke tests scheduled on gpu-cluster-staging for this branch :rocket:
Ashley: action items: Erin to produce a 3x3 matrix of (B,S,H,D) x layout x kernel perf; Tom to prototype KernelPolicy config and hot-reload; Priya to validate alignment requirements and document ABI constraints. target sync in 4 days.
Erin: noted, will post benchmarks in this thread when done :eyes:
Tom: I'll add the config proto to runtime repo. rough sketch:
```
kernel_policy:
  - name: fused_qkv
    prefer_for: {max_seq_len: 512, head_dim: 64}
  - name: per_head_stride
    fallback: true
    preserve_layout: false
```
Ashley: thanks all. be explicit about regression cases (small-batch low-latency) in the benchmarks so ops can set safe defaults for hosted tier.
Priya: added a small checklist in the shared doc for ABI checks (alignment, padding, stride multiples) — will link after lunch :link:
Erin: linking results: https://redwood-internal/bench/mha-layout-sweep (WIP)
Ashley: cool. tagging for review: @Dave @Tom @Priya. :thumbsup:
